slides.headline: India's highest cinema honor went to a director who never chased a single award.
The Dadasaheb Phalke Award, presented
slides.body: At the 47th National Film Awards ceremony at Vigyan Bhawan, New Delhi on September 18, 2000, President K.R. Narayanan presented filmmaker Hrishikesh Mukherjee with the Dadasaheb Phalke Award - India's highest honor in cinema.

slides.headline: Decades of films that never needed spectacle.
slides.body: Mukherjee's films - Anand, Anupama, Chupke Chupke, Golmaal - built entire careers on quiet, character-driven stories rather than scale. The award came with a Swarna Kamal, one lakh rupees, and a shawl.

slides.eyebrow: Why it matters for Viksit Bharat 2047
slides.headline: A body of work outlasted the moment it was made in.
slides.body: Decades after their release, Mukherjee's films are still watched, still quoted, still taught. The award wasn't for one performance - it was for a career's worth of choosing substance over noise.
